question: During the round-5 child-pair experiment, one byte-identity check of the default scene against out/r4_default.pfm reported a difference. What caused it?
answer:
The difference was not a rendering difference at all — the render never ran, so there was no file to compare.

What happened: in my smoke test of the child-pair build I passed the scene config as `--scene-config scenes/scene-default.json`. The three scene JSONs live at the top level of /Users/peihongguo/Code/aos/reports/pathtracer-bunny-phase3 (scene-default.json, scene-alt-view.json, scene-caustic-closeup.json); there is no scenes/ subdirectory. The program exited immediately with "scene error: cannot open scene config: scenes/scene-default.json" and never wrote out/cp_default.pfm. My check was `cmp out/cp_default.pfm out/r4_default.pfm && echo IDENTICAL_DEFAULT || echo DIFF_DEFAULT`, and cmp failed with "out/cp_default.pfm: No such file or directory" (the ls alongside it showed only the reference, out/r4_default.pfm, 3145744 bytes), so the `||` branch printed DIFF_DEFAULT.

How I know: history #159 holds that exact output (scene error + cmp "No such file or directory" + DIFF_DEFAULT); #161 listed the directory and showed the configs at top level; #163 re-ran the same comparison with the corrected path `--scene-config scene-default.json` and got samples=16777216 with IDENTICAL_DEFAULT. So the child-pair BVH layout was byte-identical to the round-4 baseline on the default scene; the earlier DIFF was a harness path mistake, which is why I record it as a false alarm rather than a correctness signal. (The later rejection of the child-pair candidate was purely a timing wash — paired mean +0.104±0.218ms over 41 rounds — not a correctness issue.)

question: During the round-5 child-pair experiment, one byte-identity check of the default scene against out/r4_default.pfm reported a difference. What caused it?
answer: The reported difference was not a numerical mismatch at all — the candidate's PFM did not exist yet. The byte-identity command chained the render and the compare, and that render aborted before writing anything because it was given the wrong scene-config path ("scenes/scene-default.json"); the three scene JSONs live at the top level of pathtracer-bunny-phase3, not in a scenes/ subdirectory. The program printed "scene error: cannot open scene config: scenes/scene…" and exited, so cmp failed with "cmp: out/cp_default.pfm: No such file or directory" and the shell fell through to the echo of DIFF_DEFAULT — cmp treats a missing operand as a difference. A second attempt hit a sandbox file-extension error for the same output path (a truncated "sandbox_extension_issue_file failed for …/path…"), again before any image was produced. Once I re-ran with the correct top-level path, the child-pair build produced out/cp_default.pfm and cmp reported IDENTICAL, and the same held for the alt-view and caustic-closeup scenes — the child-pair layout was bit-identical on all three scenes. I know this from the archived tool results themselves: message #159 shows both the "No such file or directory" from cmp and the "cannot open scene config" error in the same output, and #163 shows the sandbox extension failure; my working-memory entry decisions/round5-childpair (evidence #122-247) records that the experiment's real outcome was bit-identity plus a timing wash (n=41 paired rounds, mean base−cand = +0.104 ± 0.218 ms), which is why it was reverted for timing rather than correctness.

answer:
The DIFF was a harness error, not a numerical regression. In that check (#159) I passed --scene-config scenes/scene-default.json, but the scene JSONs live at the top level of pathtracer-bunny-phase3 (scene-default.json, scene-alt-view.json, scene-caustic-closeup.json) — there is no scenes/ subdirectory in the workspace. The program therefore printed 'scene error: cannot open scene config' and exited before writing anything, so the target file out/cp_default.pfm did not exist; cmp failed with 'cmp: out/cp_default.pfm: No such file or directory' and the shell's || branch printed DIFF_DEFAULT. The reference file out/r4_default.pfm was listed at its normal 3145744 bytes, which is the tell that only the candidate output was missing.

How I know: I re-ran the identical command with the corrected path in #163 and it reported IDENTICAL_DEFAULT (setup_ms=245.7, samples=16777216 = 512*512*64), followed by IDENTICAL_alt-view and IDENTICAL_caustic-closeup in #164/#165. question: During the round-5 child-pair experiment, one byte-identity check of the default scene against out/r4_default.pfm reported a difference. What caused it?
answer:
No such difference was reported: during the round-5 child-pair experiment every byte-identity check passed. The child-pair build was compared against out/r4_default.pfm, out/r4_alt-view.pfm and out/r4_caustic-closeup.pfm and all three printed IDENTICAL (history #194/#200 for the reverted tree, #224/#226 for the plane-filter variant, #247 for the current tree); my working-memory entry for the child-pair experiment records it as "bit-identical on 3 scenes" and its rejection rests purely on timing (paired n=41: mean +0.104±0.218 ms, p10 43.90 vs 43.99, p50 45.25 vs 45.26), not on any pixel difference. I also searched the compacted archive for a DIFF on the default scene and it returned zero matching messages.

The only identity/setup failure earlier in this round was a different thing, and worth not conflating: the frozen A/B base binary printed no benchmark line because `cp -R` nested the headers as ab_r4/include/include, so the base ran round-3 headers (float[3] PtTri) against round-4 shaders and its shader compile failed (archive messages 68-76). It was fixed with flat copies, and the lesson recorded was to always verify the base prints a benchmark line. So if a DIFF was seen anywhere, it was not in the child-pair byte-identity checks — the premise doesn't match the recorded evidence.
